verdictNote: Revision 3 resolves D2-1..D2-7 as round 2 required or as R2-A..R2-C ruled. No D1 finding regresses. Re-run on paper, none of the 44 earlier attack cases and none of the 23 new ones passes wrongly (18 refused, 5 residual). The two MINOR findings are precision and feasibility text. D3-1 is the gate's start time and clock. D3-2 is the image and artifactDigest wording of the residuals. Apply both in the contract build (candidate 1) and check them in its first review round. D3-2 (b) touches R2-C's wording, so it goes to the monitor. The NOTEs can be carried into the build.

round2.note: Section 3 now has a capture gate rule. Each gated value (mutationBroker, the network document and networkEnforcementDigest, hostPreflightDigest) is checked at every I01 answer against the latest completed set's required slots, with a 90 s bound on that set's scheduled start (R2-A). A later set without the slots withdraws the values at once. Sections 4.6, 5.3, 5.4 and 11 point to the rule, and section 9 adds the passing-then-failing vector and the 90 s / 90 s + 1 ms vector. The R10 facts hold: the view is replaced wholesale when a set ends (R10:obs/capture.rs:1243, :1333), every slot is reset first (:1261), and the set runs synchronously (R10:obs/observe.rs:38-40, :1386-1393). The start time and the clock behind the bound are D3-1.

R-BROKER-LIVE now lists executableLabel, listenEndpointIds and outboundEndpointIds, each with a check. R-NET-AGENT (R2-C) names the agent's executableLabel, artifactDigest and apiIdentities, keeps them in the document and gives each a check. What R-NET-AGENT still leaves out (the running image) and how its artifactDigest check fits R2-C's wording are D3-2.

The subject key is B1's: the ServiceAccount username form, with a RoleBinding's default namespace (checked at R10:obs/rbac.rs:202-219). Both documents have the entry shape {kind, name, exists, effectiveRules}. 'Every subject' means every subject a binding names. Non-resource entries take their binding's scope (R2-B). Both vectors are added. The citation for exists is off (D3-6), and B1's refusal domain is not stated for the reference model (D3-3).

R-PSA-CONFIG names the PodSecurity defaults and exemptions in the SC05 file and gives a T04 comparison. Pod Security labels on other namespaces are stated to be outside the I01 binding (I06 v2 N6, carried to W02f and W02e), both in section 4.1 and under 'Not residuals'. The T04 reference 'the enrolled file' could name its record member (D3-5).

Any listed ValidatingAdmissionPolicy or binding whose name is not one of the eight rendered names now refuses. Nothing rests on the suffix, and suffix reservation is added to R-ADM-LIST's T04 check. The vector is added. The rule is not keyed by kind (D3-4).

Named ports refuse (section 4.4). Overlapping ipBlocks are explained under R-NET-DATAPATH, and section 4.4 notes that the default-deny binding makes any rule change the digest. The vector is added. Absent port and endPort are not addressed (D3-5).

The magnitude bound now cites VPC (HO:VPC:113-114, abs(value) <= 2^53 - 1 confirmed), and R10's 0..2^53 - 1 is attributed to the configuration. A vector accepts a negative integer within the bound. OR06 is mirrored with the eight rendered names allowed, citing R10:obs/operational.rs:144-153. K19 is described as the only NetworkPolicy form in I07 v3's vectors.

round1Regressions.note: Round 2 found it partly resolved because the gates were anchored to the snapshot. The per-answer gate (D2-1) closes that: a set that fails after the snapshot withdraws the gated values. Clock and start time: D3-1.

Round 2 found it partly resolved because R-BROKER-LIVE missed members and the network agent had no residual. Both are now named (D2-2, R2-C). The precision of the image wording is D3-2, which is new and not a regression.

findings.location: DESIGN 3 (the capture gate rule), 1 (the owner's frame), 9 (the 90 s vector), 11
findings.finding: The gate compares 'that set's scheduled start' with the answer, but R10's capture engine does not hold that value. capture_set takes the scheduled start as a parameter (a monotonic Instant, R10:obs/capture.rs:276, :1241), and the view stores only sequence, the slots and set_started_ms, the wall clock at the set's actual start (:242, :1250). The epoch's cycle_scheduled is overwritten when the next cycle starts (R10:obs/observe.rs:1166). That happens before the cycle's progress read and scrape, and I01 is served during both. It also stays advanced when that scrape escalates and takes no set (:1319-1323, :1386-1393). A port that read cycle_scheduled would pair a newer schedule with an older view, stretching the bound to about 150 s after an escalated cycle. The design also names no clock. The only start the view stores is wall time: a port that compared it with the answer's wall time would accept a stale set after a backward clock step. R10 already guards its expiry against exactly that step with a latch (R10:obs/observe.rs:47-49, :490-499). A gate on the monotonic clock alone would not count a host suspend (Rust's Instant on Linux; general knowledge, not a pinned source). So for this input, section 1's 'one its capture engine already holds' is not accurate. Implementing the gate needs no new permission and no new read, only one stored field. The I01 service would also have to be handed the view, since it receives only wall and now (R10:obs/client.rs:270-283).
findings.requiredChange: State that the gate's start is the latest completed set's own scheduled start, recorded with that set (R10 adds it to the view beside the slots), and never the epoch's current cycle_scheduled. Name the clock: the monotonic clock of the scheduled Instant. Also fail closed when the wall age (answer wall time minus set_started_ms) is negative or over 90 s, so that neither clock's step or freeze can make an old set look young. Correct section 1's frame sentence for this input. Add vectors for a cycle whose scrape escalates after cycle_scheduled advanced (refuses once the latest set's own start is over 90 s old) and for a wall clock stepped back by more than 90 s (refuses).

findings.finding: (a) R-NET-AGENT leaves out the agent's running image. check_backend_capture is ENTRY_BOUND, 'domain entry plus the measured file, not the running image' (R10:obs/capture_check.rs:613; HO:NP4R:137-139). It measures the file at executable and binds the process only by processLabel and cgroupPath. Native-profile v4 itself names the gap: there is no execute_no_trans closure for the qualk8s sources, which goes to a matrix successor plus T04 (HO:NP4R:253-258). (b) R2-C asks for R-NET-AGENT 'with its three T04 checks', and the owner's frame asks for a T04 check per residual. For artifactDigest, though, the design gives 'HE-008's off-host enrollment measurement', which is not a T04 check. (c) In effect, artifactDigest is not unobserved. check_record's artifact custody requires a component's artifactDigest to equal the sha256 of its executable's backendFiles row (R10:obs/record_check.rs:589-594, :915). Each set's backend capture compares the live file's contentDigest and verity with that row (R10:obs/capture_check.rs:630-634). For a record that passed check_record at enrollment, artifactDigest is therefore the file content measured every set. The observer itself does not run check_record (R10:obs/enrolled.rs:17-18). (d) R-BROKER-LIVE assigns the broker image's binding to T04-LABELS. LABEL_BOUND's premises, however, are T04-ENTRYPOINT (P-a) and T04-ENTRYPOINT-CENSUS (P-b) (HO:NP4R:116-130, :319-320), while T04-LABELS covers only declared labels (:325). This text is carried over from rev 2.
findings.requiredChange: Add to R-NET-AGENT: 'the running image (ENTRY_BOUND: domain entry plus the measured file; HO:NP4R:137-139, :253-258)', with T04-ENTRYPOINT, T04-ENTRYPOINT-CENSUS and the matrix successor's execute_no_trans closure as its checks. For artifactDigest, give a T04 check as R2-C's wording asks, for example 'the running agent's executable content equals the record's artifactDigest', and cite the custody link. Proposing to drop it from the residual instead would change R2-C and goes to the monitor. In R-BROKER-LIVE, name T04-ENTRYPOINT and T04-ENTRYPOINT-CENSUS for the image's binding.

findings.finding: Section 4.5 adopts B1's subject key but does not say that the RBAC documents' inputs are refused wherever B1 refuses. B1 refuses: a ClusterRoleBinding ServiceAccount subject without a namespace (R10:obs/rbac.rs:212-214); an unknown subject kind (:192-197); a roleRef outside the RBAC group, or a ClusterRoleBinding naming a Role (:225-240); a dangling roleRef (:313-315); a rule with nonResourceURLs beside resources (:141-143); and a non-resource rule bound to the loopback user (:319-322). B1 also reads an empty subject namespace as absent (:207). The observer refuses all of these before any document exists, because produce_snapshot runs before Closure::check (R10:obs/observe.rs:14-15). The harness-onion reference model is written independently, though. If it computed bytes for such a cluster, HE-008 could sign values that the observer never reproduces. That fails closed, but the replay vectors would disagree. 'Non-resource rule' is also not defined; B1's meaning is a non-empty nonResourceURLs list (:133, :139).
findings.requiredChange: State that the model refuses exactly B1's refusals, listed with B1's lines, before computing either RBAC document. Define a non-resource rule as B1 does. Add a vector for a ClusterRoleBinding ServiceAccount subject without a namespace.

findings.finding: The exact-name rule does not consider kind. Under 'whose name is not one of the eight rendered names', a ValidatingAdmissionPolicy may carry a rendered binding's name, for example planeon-a2-pod-binding.static.k8s.io. The eight rendered names are all distinct and all end in .static.k8s.io (checked in planeon-a2.json). A listed object with a rendered name is also never compared with the rendered object. So an API-created object that takes a rendered name rests entirely on R-ADM-LIST's suffix-reservation T04 check. It can only add denials.
findings.requiredChange: State the rule over (kind, name): the four policy names for ValidatingAdmissionPolicy and the four binding names for ValidatingAdmissionPolicyBinding. Say that a listed object with a rendered (kind, name) is covered by R-ADM-LIST's suffix check.

findings.finding: Three points of wording. (1) 'every port ... is an integer' does not say what happens to a ports entry with no port (all ports), or to endPort. Both are label-free, and any rule changes the digest against the default-deny binding, so nothing passes wrongly. But the model and the port could still differ between a form refusal and a digest mismatch, and the refusal texts are pinned in the vectors. A port written as a string of digits is a JSON string, so it refuses either way. (2) R-PSA-CONFIG's T04 compares 'the running PodSecurity configuration' with 'the enrolled file's' without naming the record member that pins that file. The v4 schema allows a 0444 backendFiles row with zero segments, and no harness-onion text names the file beyond SC05. (3) R-BROKER-LIVE's endpoint check says 'the signed ones'. It could say the record's listenEndpointIds and outboundEndpointIds, resolved through the enrolled endpoint tuples.
findings.requiredChange: Say whether an absent port and an integer endPort are admitted, and add one vector. Name R-PSA-CONFIG's reference, for example the APISERVER backendFiles row for the SC05 file, or the release's sealed copy. Make the endpoint check's reference explicit.

findings.finding: The citation 'exists as B1 defines it (R10:obs/rbac.rs:243-256)' points at produce_snapshot's doc comment and its list fetches. B1 defines exists at :272-278 (the listed ServiceAccounts) and :325-328: true for User and Group, and for a ServiceAccount, whether that ServiceAccount is listed.
findings.requiredChange: Cite R10:obs/rbac.rs:272-278 and :325-328, and state the rule in one line.

findings.finding: The gated values reflect the latest set. A host change is therefore seen only at the next set, and an answer can carry gated values for up to about 90 s after the change. A change that is reverted between two sets is never seen. R2-A accepted this bound ('a late set refuses and costs only availability'), but the design states only the availability side, not that this sampling window exists.
findings.requiredChange: Add one sentence to section 3 stating the sampling window as R2-A's accepted bound, and that T04 and HE-005 cover persistent state only. No residual is needed if the monitor agrees that R2-A covers it.

adversarialCases.case: A set that fails between two answers
adversarialCases.where: 3: the view is replaced wholesale when a set ends (R10:obs/capture.rs:1243, :1333), and the gate is checked at every answer, so the second answer refuses; section 9 vector

adversarialCases.case: A cycle whose scrape escalates, so it takes no set (R10:obs/observe.rs:1319-1323)
adversarialCases.where: 3: refuses once the latest set's own scheduled start is more than 90 s old; before that, the earlier set's verdicts stand within R2-A's bound. Only a port that read the epoch's already-advanced cycle_scheduled (:1166) would stretch this: D3-1.

adversarialCases.case: A re-snapshot of up to 120 s, during which no cycle runs while I01 is served in the client's waits
adversarialCases.where: 3: the 90 s bound withdraws the gated values; this costs availability only

adversarialCases.case: Wall clock stepped back by more than 90 s after the latest set, while sets have stopped
adversarialCases.where: Only because the 'scheduled start' is R10's monotonic Instant. The design names no clock, and the only start R10's view stores, set_started_ms, is wall time: a port that used it would pass a stale set (D3-1).

adversarialCases.case: Wall clock stepped forward past the record's expiresAt - 3 s or past the 90 s bound
adversarialCases.where: Expiry latches (R10:obs/observe.rs:490-499); otherwise the cost is availability only

adversarialCases.case: An answer served while a set runs
adversarialCases.where: Not possible. The observer is single-threaded: there is no thread spawn in the observer sources (pruned git grep -l, no hits), and I01 is served only inside the client's waits (R10:obs/client.rs:22-26). The set runs inside the scrape answer's handler (R10:obs/observe.rs:1386-1393) and readers see the old view until the set ends.

adversarialCases.case: A host change between two sets, or one reverted before the next set
adversarialCases.where: This sampling window is accepted by R2-A's 90 s bound but is not stated in the design (D3-7)

adversarialCases.case: A renamed static admission object
adversarialCases.where: 4.1: the rendered hash must equal the pin and ADM-4's loaded hash, and any listed name outside the eight refuses

adversarialCases.case: An API-registered object, created before the guard, that takes one of the eight rendered names, or a policy carrying a rendered binding's name
adversarialCases.where: R-ADM-LIST's suffix-reservation T04 check. Listed content is not compared, and the rule ignores kind (D3-4). Such an object can only add denials.

adversarialCases.case: A binding whose policyName points elsewhere
adversarialCases.where: A static binding: the rendered hash. An API binding with a name outside the eight: the exact-name rule. An API binding with a rendered name: the residual case above.

adversarialCases.case: A ServiceAccount subject with a namespace
adversarialCases.where: 4.5: key system:serviceaccount:<ns>:<name> (R10:obs/rbac.rs:217), so any change changes the bytes

adversarialCases.case: A ServiceAccount subject without a namespace (RoleBinding; ClusterRoleBinding; empty string)
adversarialCases.where: RoleBinding: the binding's namespace. ClusterRoleBinding: B1 refuses before any document (R10:obs/rbac.rs:212-214). An empty string counts as absent (:207). The reference model's matching rule is not stated: D3-3.

adversarialCases.case: A Group or User subject, including a User named with a ServiceAccount's username
adversarialCases.where: Keyed by (kind, raw name); a grant moved between kinds or names changes both digests

adversarialCases.case: A non-resource rule granted through a RoleBinding in the qualification namespace
adversarialCases.where: R2-B: scope is the qualification namespace, so the entry is in rbac and in the closure. It is inert for the authorizer, and any change fails closed.

adversarialCases.case: A NetworkPolicy port with endPort
adversarialCases.where: Admitted by 4.4, but the digest changes against the default-deny binding (wording: D3-5)

adversarialCases.case: A NetworkPolicy port given as a string of digits
adversarialCases.where: 4.4: a JSON string is not an integer, so it is a selector form outside v1

adversarialCases.case: A NetworkPolicy ports entry with no port
adversarialCases.where: Either a form refusal or a digest change against the default-deny binding (wording: D3-5)

adversarialCases.case: R-PSA-CONFIG: is it precise enough for T04?
adversarialCases.where: It names the SC05 file and a comparison. The reference's record member is unnamed (D3-5).

adversarialCases.case: The network agent's running image differs from the measured executable (an old image still running, or another entry-typed file)
adversarialCases.where: ENTRY_BOUND does not bind the running image (HO:NP4R:137-139, :253-258). R-NET-DATAPATH's ruleset and flag T04 covers behaviour, but R-NET-AGENT does not name the image (D3-2).

adversarialCases.case: The network agent's executable file replaced (content differs from the record)
adversarialCases.where: The backend capture compares contentDigest and verity with the backendFiles row (R10:obs/capture_check.rs:630-634); check_record's custody binds that row to artifactDigest (R10:obs/record_check.rs:592-594)

adversarialCases.case: R-BROKER-LIVE additions: are they precise enough for T04?
adversarialCases.where: executableLabel and the endpoint ids are named with checks. The image proof should be T04-ENTRYPOINT and -CENSUS (D3-2), and the endpoint reference could be explicit (D3-5).

adversarialCases.case: Echo path anywhere in revision 3
adversarialCases.where: None found. Real projections and RBAC come from live lists, and admissionPolicy is tied to ADM-4's loaded hash. The record-derived gated values are named residuals behind the per-answer gate, the binding is only compared against, and uids and synthetic identities are contract derivations.

adversarialCases.case: A gated value served from a set taken under another record
adversarialCases.where: The record is immutable for the epoch (R10:obs/enrolled.rs:15), and each capture binds qualificationDigest (R10:obs/capture_check.rs:346-348, :619)
